A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robustness study, with matching title, authors, methods and experiments. All seven pages of v1 and ten pages of v2, including appendices, figures and tables, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of twelve language models on WTQ and TAT-QA, including prompting, model-size and perturbation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original WTQ and TAT-QA evaluations and adds SciTab results, robustness measurements and table-size analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same structural perturbations, GPT-3.5-generated datatype-preserving replacements, fixed-string replacements, answer removal and no-table procedure. Renaming VP to ValP and expanding the generation explanation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds SciTab scientific claim verification, presented as classification in a question-answering format, alongside WTQ and TAT-QA. Its scientific domain and compositional claim-reasoning requirements substantially extend coverage. Figure 4 and Table 4 report actual structural-perturbation and no-table evaluations.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve Llama2, Llama3 and Mistral/Mixtral base, chat and instruction variants listed in Table 3. Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding WTQ and TAT-QA comparisons. Newly cited TableFormer and FREB-TQA are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: v2 expands evaluation beyond EM by adding exact-match difference and correctness-transition variation percentage, with results in Tables 1 and 4. It also reports table-size-stratified evaluations and explicitly pools few-shot comparisons across three datasets. The WTQ/TAT-QA sample counts remain unchanged; 3-shot evaluation already appears in v1 Figure 10, despite its omission from the earlier prose.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Figure 10 add a focused sensitivity analysis of performance versus table size under the original condition and five structural perturbations across three datasets. The existing prompting, model-scale, instruction-tuning and perturbation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Error bars already appear in v1's model and few-shot plots and remain in v2. No new run counts, seeds, explanation of the error bars or statistical testing procedures are supplied. The new variation-percentage metric measures perturbation sensitivity, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds SciTab scores, table-size curves and VP/Emd result entries. Table 1 also revises aggregate WTQ EM: original large/small-model scores change from 0.35/0.28 to 0.36/0.25, and DVP scores from 0.20/0.16 to 0.21/0.14. Meanwhile, the WTQ/TAT-QA heatmap values are retained in the merged Figure 4. The aggregate revisions are not fully explained and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix E newly defines Emd = EMperturbed - EMorig and VP = (C2W + W2C)/N, quantities absent from v1. This is a limited addition of mathematical definitions, without new assumptions, theorems or proofs. The added standard EM formula is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the stated study to include scientific claims through SciTab. The principal contributions concerning in-context learning, instruction tuning, model scale, Wikipedia-related bias and insufficient practical reliability remain substantially unchanged, as does the conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes an important interpretation: v1 treats moderate TAT-QA EM as indicating insufficient robustness, whereas v2 interprets smaller Emd and lower VP on TAT-QA and SciTab as greater robustness than WTQ despite lower accuracy. v2 also qualifies the model-size trend with SciTab exceptions and adds interpretations concerning table complexity. The limitations paragraph is largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Figure 9 newly disclose the GPT-3.5 system/user prompt for datatype-preserving fake answers and expand the generation explanation; GPT-3.5 use and answer-containing-table filtering were already documented. v2 also supplies SciTab evaluation counts and explicit small/large model thresholds without changing the existing model groups.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lu et al. (2023) on SciTab, Yang et al. (2022) on TableFormer and Zhou et al. (2024) on FREB-TQA, connecting them to coverage and robustness metrics. It also clarifies the T5-based prior approach attributed to Wang et al. (2022). The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main five-section sequence and much of the prose are retained. Changes include localized grammar editing, citation-style changes, VP-to-ValP terminology, flattening the NVP/NT subheadings, expanded explanations and reorganized appendices. These do not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 merges v1's separate WTQ and TAT-QA heatmaps into a three-dataset Figure 4, expands Table 1 to include three metrics, and adds the comprehensive Table 4. It also adds table-size and dataset-specific plots and redraws few-shot displays. The original four prompt examples are retained and renumbered as Figures 5–8. This substantially reworks the empirical presentation.

improvement.justification: SciTab coverage, explicit robustness metrics, table-size analysis and the disclosed generation prompt improve the empirical assessment and reproducibility. They provide a better basis for distinguishing accuracy from perturbation sensitivity. However, aggregate-score revisions remain unexplained, large-model WTQ no-table EM differs between Tables 1 and 4 (0.05 versus 0.06), and Appendix F's baseline comparison conflicts with Figure 10. These reporting problems limit the overall gain.
